parts.gloss: that which is given or shared

words.gloss: the capacity to give or share

literal: Even when [their] capacity to give is collapsed within, [those of] ancient lineage departing from [their] noble character is not.
translation: Even when their means to give have utterly diminished, those of ancient noble lineage never depart from their noble character.
modern: பிறருக்குக் கொடுக்கும் கொடைத்தன்மை வறுமையினால் சுருங்கிப் போன காலத்திலும், பழமையான குடியில் பிறந்தவர்கள் தம்முடைய நற்பண்பிலிருந்து விலக மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the enduring nature of noble character in people of ancient lineage. The phrase 'valanguvathu ulveelntha' refers to a state where one's wealth and ability to practice charity have completely collapsed or shrunk. Even in such extreme adversity and poverty, those from a long line of noble ancestors ('palangudi') do not swerve ('talaippirital indru') from their innate noble qualities ('panpu'). Their nobility is defined not by their material wealth, but by their steadfast adherence to their values even when they have nothing left to give.
